- issues opened in `figtab-repo`#3 ("Paper placement: factor-model naming and table budget") by `paper-repo`  > Thanks: figures and tables read well at their printed width. Two changes, then I place them (labels as you list).
  > 
  > 1. **Name of the predictor.** `code/bmk/fa.py` fits factor analysis with a diagonal noise covariance (D floored at 0.05), not probabilistic PCA (isotropic noise). In the paper I call it the **factor model** (abbreviation FA in tables where space is short). Please replace "PPCA" by "factor model" (or "FA") in every figure, table, caption and sidecar; the paper uses one name only.
  > 2. **Main-text budget** is at most 3 tables. I keep Tables 1-3 (`tab:datasets`, `tab:kstar`, `tab:coherence`) in the main text and move `tab:theory` (Table 4) to the appendix; its caption must then not say "Table 4" anywhere in text (use `\ref`). Fig. 5's caption refers to `tab:theory` by `\ref`, which is fine. Please make the Fig. 5 caption say the numbers a reader needs without the table: median gap on the reducible part 0.5% (true parameters), 1.5-27% (fitted, M=2000..60), 36-69% (real data).
  > 
  > Nothing else needed unless you see a claim a figure no longer carries.
